title: fix(memory): handle duplicate chunk IDs during indexing
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated content can produce identical memory chunk IDs within one sync batch. PostgreSQL rejects the resulting multi-row upsert with "ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time", preventing fresh indexing, full reindex publication, and some incremental replacements. SQLite accepts those writes with last-write semantics.

## User Impact

The shared chunk writer now deduplicates each upsert in memory. Canonical content comes from the last row carrying an embedding; recall metadata and provenance come from the last row overall. A trailing metadata-only row preserves the earlier content and embedding.

Existing SQL statements, conflict-update fields, transaction boundaries, locks, schema, and vector-projection ownership are preserved. No extra database round trips or configuration changes are introduced.

## Evidence

The tests-only [baseline #179550](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179550) preserves the production writer from main. Final baseline head: f84b447401161c4f0570e3150aa1a440daad753e. Final fixed head: 2311e59b119744fb618060aefdf27ec68ab32fdd. Test source bytes are identical on both branches.

| Real memory-manager sync | PostgreSQL before | PostgreSQL after | SQLite before / after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh index | Duplicate-target error | PASS | PASS / PASS |
| Shadow/full reindex | Duplicate-target error | PASS | PASS / PASS |
| Incremental replacement | Duplicate-target error | PASS | PASS / PASS |

Every flow uses memory/repeat.md containing exactly 3,200 ASCII x characters without a newline. [Baseline manager proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629634884/job/119324948786): three genuine PG failures and matching SQLite controls. [Final fixed manager proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629349138/job/119323945422): all six cases pass, with the infra phase passing 240/240.

Native semantic cases cover two duplicates, 129 duplicates across flushes, and a trailing metadata-only row. [Baseline PG](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629634884/job/119324948664) fails all three with the actual canonical/metadata upsert SQL and conflicting synthetic inputs captured. [Fixed PG](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629349138/job/119323945497) passes all three. [Baseline SQLite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629634884/job/119324949306) and [fixed SQLite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629349138/job/119323946068) pass identical assertions for canonical text and embedding bytes, vector projection, recall metadata, and provenance.

[Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629349138) passed, including PostgreSQL conformance [1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629349138/job/119323945422), [2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629349138/job/119323945453), and [3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39629349138/job/119323945497). Earlier CI caught a test expectation using float32 for canonical binary64 storage and a missing-braces lint error; both were corrected before this green head. Independent Codex review completed without actionable P0–P2 findings, including final source-integrity verification; the assertion correction received a separate clean review. The final brace repair is formatting only.

## Scope and Limits

PR CI is the designated proof host. File preparation, chunking, manager sync, native publication, and retrieval are real; only the external embedding service is fixed to synthetic vectors. The separate CLI/Gateway/live-model harness was not run. The minimal fixture proves the soak's failure class, but the original soak did not retain its offending SQL and rows. No latency or throughput improvement is claimed.

Production delta is +15/-7 lines (net +8); tests and routing are +351/-22. The six manager cases took about 60 seconds of test time in the PG conformance job because they exercise both native engines and the three real sync lifecycles. The three native PG semantic cases took about 0.5 seconds combined. Local broad tests were avoided on the load-blocked host; formatting, whitespace, and normal commit hooks passed.
